images.caption:
Pictured is the new valve and piping system at Makah National Fish Hatchery, a project completed in August, 2010 using $89,593 in Recovery Act funding. The old systems had deteriorated to the point where inefficiencies associated with the system regularly threatened production goals, as well as the Hatchery's production commitments to the Makah Tribe. 

You are free to use this image with the following photo credit: Caroline Peterschmidt/U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

images.caption:
As part of a series of system overhauls at the Makah National Fish Hatchery, Burton Construction, Inc., refit the Hatchery's aging electrical system using $334,341 in Recovery Act funding. The work was completed in October, 2010 and significantly improves efficiency and safety at the Hatchery, eliminating regular electrical system failures produced by outdated and aging equipment. Pictured are the new primary control panels for the facility.

You are free to use this image with the following photo credit: Caroline Peterschmidt/U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

images.caption:
In conjunction with the Recovery Act-funded electrical system rehabilitation project at Makah National Fish Hatchery, Sabyr Contractors replaced and repaired a series of aging pumps in order to increase efficiency and decrease energy use. Workers are pictured here during the removal of one of the failing pumps. The project was completed in June, 2010 using $54,608 in Recovery Act funding. 

You are free to use this image with the following photo credit: Marsha McGee/U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
